final_note: Cells operate as closed sediment compartments at large scale.

concepts.def: Self-contained coastal compartment with sources, transfers and sinks; 11 in England and Wales.
Where sediment enters the cell (rivers, cliffs, offshore).
Movement via longshore drift, waves, tides.
Where sediment is deposited (beach, spit, offshore bar).
Zigzag sediment movement along coast driven by oblique wave swash.
East Yorkshire coast retreating at ~1.8 m/yr, fastest in Europe.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cell 2 runs from Flamborough Head (north) to The Wash. Holderness lies within this cell, with cliffs of weak boulder clay (till) deposited during the last glaciation. Sediment moves south to feed Spurn Head spit and offshore Humber sinks.

Cliffs of unconsolidated boulder clay retreat at 1.8 m/yr on average, locally up to 10 m/yr. Around 29 villages have been lost since Roman times. Mappleton groynes (1991) trapped sediment north but increased downdrift erosion at Cowden, illustrating cell connectivity.

Spurn Head is a 5.5 km recurved spit at the Humber mouth, formed from southward longshore drift. The neck was breached in 2013 during a tidal surge, illustrating sediment supply vulnerability when updrift cliffs are protected.
